- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment drops below 0.30 and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overpredicts mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 10-day average is >10% above 30-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 10 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.30–0.67), model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use 3-day moving average of true values as a smoothing anchor for next 7 days.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5 days, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
